item.title: SQL Server: Script to Search Text in All Columns Across All Tables
item.description:
“SQL Server: Script to Search Text in All Columns Across All Tables”

How can one effectively write a T-SQL script or stored procedure to iterate through every user-defined table and search across all designated data type columns (primarily text types) for a specific input string in a SQL Server database?

Searching for a substring or value across an entire database schema can be a complex task, often requiring dynamic SQL execution to inspect table structures and query data dynamically. Several effective methods exist, relying on system catalog views like INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES and INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS or the sys schema tables.

item.title: SQL Stored Procedure Results into Temporary Tables: Methods and Best Practices
item.description:
“SQL Stored Procedure Results into Temporary Tables: Methods and Best Practices”

When working with SQL Server, there are several scenarios where you need to execute a stored procedure and then utilize its returned data within a temporary table. This is common for data manipulation, reporting, or when integrating stored procedure output into other SQL queries. This question explores various methods to achieve this, offering different approaches based on SQL Server versions and specific requirements.
